name: Mucorales spp. — mucormycosis

syndromes.title: Adults — all treatment modalities and antifungal drugs available (Figure 5A)
rows: 5–10 mg/kg/dayay IV; 10 mg/kg/dayay for brain involvement
Weeks to months; continue until reversal of immunosuppression and imaging/clinical response
Perform early complete surgical debridement whenever feasible; consider step-down/salvage with ISA or PCZ
Source Figure 5A is the preferred full-resource adult pathway.
Surgery and antifungal therapy should proceed together when feasible.
ISA 200 mg TID d1–2 → 200 mg/day; PCZ 300 mg BID d1 → 300 mg/day
Moderately recommended first-line/strong salvage depending agent and context
Use as step-down/salvage when clinically appropriate
Exact recommendation strength differs by route/formulation and context. Formulation matters for posaconazole dosing; verify the cited source formulation.

syndromes.title: Adults — amphotericin B lipid formulations are not available (Figure 5B)
rows: ISA 200 mg TID d1–2 → 200 mg/day; PCZ DR/IV 300 mg BID d1 → 300 mg/day
Adult mucormycosis where lipid AmB formulations are unavailable
Use the source's alternative resource pathway
This is a distinct source pathway and is not interchangeable with the full-resource pathway.
Amphotericin B deoxycholate only when safer lipid formulations are unavailable and alternatives cannot be used
Recommended against in usual settings because of toxicity; fallback only
Included to preserve resource-availability logic, not to promote AmB-d as preferred therapy.

syndromes.title: Adults — isavuconazole and posaconazole IV/DR are not available (Figure 5C)
rows: 5–10 mg/kg/dayay IV; 10 mg/kg/dayay for brain involvement
Adult mucormycosis without ISA or PCZ IV/DR access
Continue surgery/source control; use available oral formulations only where supported
This branch preserves the source's distinct pathway when the newer triazole formulations are unavailable.

overview: Syndrome-level hub summarizing adult and paediatric treatment pathways from the uploaded global mucormycosis guideline.
notes: Species cards inherit these Mucorales-level recommendations unless species-specific evidence is explicitly stated.
source_note: Different L-AmB doses reflect CNS involvement, resource pathway, SOT/renal context and paediatric considerations; retain branch context.
normalization_note: Dose notation: LD=loading dose; q24h=daily; BID=twice daily; TID=three times daily; QID=four times daily; PO=oral; IV=intravenous. Formulation-specific azole doses must not be interchanged.

audit_summary.visual_status: All SVGs are summary reconstructions; original guideline figure remains definitive
audit_summary.population_scope: Adults + guideline-specific paediatric/neonatal sections where explicitly covered
